Reviewed parallel cell metadata showing actual parallel use, three subagents, artifact files fraction.mjs/test20.mjs/cli.mjs, and failed official solution status despite 141 of 146 passing.
Reviewed completed official parallel status, protocol validation with AgentSwarm plus direct Agent, artifact validation, and evaluator result of 141/146 with solution_passed false.
Reviewed official evaluator summary confirming completed run, expected 146 cases, pass rate 0.9657534246575342, and solution_passed false.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream accounted for session creation, prompt delivery, subagent starts and completions, parent file reads, final response, and clean prompt completion.
Session index mapped the parallel Kimi session id to the workspace session directory for the raw actor files.
Fraction-library child received the Number-only rational brief, wrote /output/fraction.mjs, ran local unit checks, and reported a Number-backed Fraction API.
CLI child received a separate parser brief, wrote /output/cli.mjs, tested parsing and argparse-style errors, and reported the parseArgs API.
Entry-file child read the two libraries, wrote /output/test20.mjs, verified the four samples plus small extra cases, and reported byte-identical visible outputs.
Parallel parent probed the executable, launched an AgentSwarm for fraction and CLI modules, delegated entry integration, read the final files, and returned a completion summary.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Reviewed the same Python fractions migration prompt with the exact precision, CLI, ESM, .mjs, zero external dependency, and executable-only observation requirements.
Reviewed serial cell metadata showing no subagents, artifact files test20.mjs/lib/fraction.mjs/lib/argparser.mjs, and official solution_passed true.
Reviewed completed official serial status, artifact validation, no parallel control violation, and evaluator result of 146/146 with solution_passed true.
Reviewed official evaluator summary confirming completed run, expected 146 cases, pass rate 1.0, and solution_passed true.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream accounted for the single main-agent session, file writes, verification commands, final response, and clean prompt completion.
Session index mapped the serial Kimi session id to the workspace session directory for the raw main actor file.
Serial main actor implemented the fraction library, parser, and entry file locally, used BigInt-backed exact arithmetic, tested samples and a 21-digit case, and finished successfully.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the ESM, .mjs, no external dependency, CLI parity, output parity, and executable-probing requirements, but converted the precision requirement into a child-facing assertion that Number arithmetic was safe.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first probed behavior, then split ownership among a fraction child, a CLI child, and a later entry/integration child, while the parent retained overall orchestration and final response.
parallel.implementation: Agent-0 wrote a root-level Number-backed Fraction class, agent-1 wrote a root-level parseArgs module, and agent-2 wrote test20.mjs importing those two modules and computing the required sums, products, means, and comparisons.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The entry child consumed the two module APIs and wrote the final entry file; artifact validation later found fraction.mjs, cli.mjs, and test20.mjs in the delivered directory.
parallel.verification: Parallel verification covered the four sample cases, parser error checks, zero-reciprocal behavior, and several small or million-scale extra cases, but did not catch the official hidden precision failures.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final artifact used regular Number arithmetic for fraction numerators and denominators, so it failed five official test cases requiring exact Python Fraction behavior beyond those checks.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same ESM, .mjs, CLI, output, and exact Fraction behavior obligations, and explicitly treated exact rational arithmetic as requiring arbitrary-precision integer storage.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single main actor owned the full pipeline: inspect/probe, fraction library, argparse mimic, entry file, verification, and final delivery without subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote lib/fraction.mjs with BigInt-backed normalized rational arithmetic, lib/argparser.mjs for the six options, and test20.mjs using those modules for all required operations.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The same actor integrated the library and parser under a lib directory, wrote the entry point with explicit .mjs imports, and artifact validation found the expected delivered files.
serial.verification: The serial actor ran the four samples, edge cases, error cases, zero division behavior, and a 21-digit integer input that exceeded double precision, all matching the executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible in the trajectory; the official evaluator completed and accepted all 146 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel preserved most surface requirements but passed the fraction child a narrowed precision assumption using Number arithmetic.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial handled the same output-parity requirement as exact rational arithmetic and implemented arbitrary-precision storage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material difference was the interpretation and transfer of the exact numerical precision obligation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed by module: fraction library, CLI parser, and entry/integration were assigned to different actors.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept implementation, integration, and verification under the single main actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a context boundary for the fraction representation, while serial kept that decision with the implementer and verifier.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The fraction child received a detailed API contract but also the misleading context that BigInt was prohibited and Number precision was safe.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child context transfer and retained the exact-precision reasoning through implementation and testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The interface itself worked; the missing task context was the robust precision obligation for hidden inputs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel's delivered fraction module used Math.abs, %, division, and stored num/den as regular Numbers.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a BigInt-backed fraction module and used BigInt literals in the entry computations.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The arithmetic representation differed, and that difference explains the official hidden precision failures.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All delegated children completed and their summaries returned; the parent then read the delivered files before final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle because the main actor performed all work locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The lifecycle completed, so the failure is not an unjoined or trapped child result; it is the content of the fraction child result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate root-level files and the entry child imported them with explicit .mjs suffixes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a lib directory plus entry file, all by the same actor, with explicit .mjs imports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No collision or overwrite explains the outcome; the integrated parallel files were coherent but numerically inexact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified the four samples and several extra cases that stayed within Number-safe ranges, then accepted the result.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the four samples plus a 21-digit numerator case specifically exceeding double precision, along with other error and edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification covered the precision risk that parallel's child brief had ruled out.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used more wall time, requests, tools, and tokens, but did not time out and closed with all children complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with fewer requests and no subagents, then passed the official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget pressure is not the causal difference; closure was timely in both modes, but parallel closed on an inexact delegated implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official result is discordant because the parallel artifact used Number-backed rational arithmetic created by a delegated fraction child, while the serial artifact used BigInt-backed exact rational arithmetic and tested a 21-digit case. The parallel checks matched visible samples and small extras, but the official evaluator exposed five precision-sensitive failures; the serial run's exact implementation passed all 146 cases.
parallel_contributors: The parent delegated the fraction library with a child brief that said BigInt was prohibited and Number precision was safe, narrowing the original exact-output obligation.
The fraction child followed that brief and produced Number numerator/denominator storage, which the parent later read and accepted.
Parallel verification did not include a true arbitrary-precision stress case comparable to the serial 21-digit input.
serial_contributors: The serial actor kept the precision decision in one context and implemented BigInt-backed exact rational arithmetic.
The serial actor verified a huge integer case beyond double precision before finalizing.
The official serial status shows a completed 146/146 pass.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The parallel and serial directory layouts differed, but both were accepted as artifacts and this does not explain the score gap.
CLI implementation details differed, but both runs tested argparse-style behavior and no evidence ties CLI parsing to the failed official cases.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator identifies only aggregate 141/146 versus 146/146 in the mounted status, so exact hidden failing inputs are not visible in this pair.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
